learningObjective: Understand mma.sync as warp-cooperative with register-fragment operand layout.

canonicalClaims.claim: Tensor Core `mma.sync` is a warp-cooperative instruction that executes one matrix multiply-add whose operand tiles are distributed across the 32 lanes' registers in a hardware-defined fragment layout; individual lanes hold only fragments.
conditions: Ampere+ Tensor Core / mma.sync as documented in PTX ISA.
nonImplications: Does not imply lane-level independent MMAs.
Does not imply GMEM/SMEM can be operands directly.

misconceptions.claim: Each of the 32 lanes runs its own independent mma.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The mma is warp-cooperative; the tile is shared across lanes.
Operands must be in registers; ldmatrix loads them from SMEM.
Programmers/libraries emit it explicitly (CUTLASS, cuBLAS internals).

misconceptions.claim: All mma shapes use the same register fragment layout.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Layout is defined per m/n/k tuple in PTX ISA.

implementationFacts: Common shapes: m16n8k8 (fp16), m16n8k16 (fp16), m16n8k16/m16n8k32 (int8), m16n8k8 (tf32).
`ldmatrix.sync` loads a 4x4/8x8 tile from SMEM into the mma fragment layout.
